{{Short description|German biochemist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2024}}
'''Johannes Buchner''' is a German biochemist and professor at the [[Technical University of Munich]], Munich, Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.department.ch.tum.de/biotech/startseite/|title=Startseite – Lehrstuhl für Biotechnologie|website=www.department.ch.tum.de|accessdate=27 November 2021}}</ref>

== Career ==

Buchner obtained his PhD at the university of [[Regensburg]], Germany, working with Rainer Rudolph and Rainer Jaenicke. He performed his postdoctoral research in the lab of [[Ira Pastan]] at the [[National Cancer Institute]] of the [[National Institutes of Health]] in Bethesda, USA, before becoming assistant professor at the University of Regensburg and subsequently full professor and Chair of [[Biotechnology]] at the TUM.

==Research==
Molecular [[Chaperone (protein)|chaperones]] are an essential class of [[protein]]s that aid other proteins to obtain their biologically active structure and inhibit off-pathway side reactions during protein maturation.<ref name="Buchner 2005 p. ">{{cite book | last=Buchner | first=Johannes | title=Protein folding handbook | publisher=Wiley-VCH | publication-place=Weinheim | year=2005 | isbn=978-3-527-30784-5 | oclc=214281963 | language=de | page=}}</ref> Buchner's work focuses on understanding mechanisms of molecular chaperones in a quantitative and mechanistic manner. His work has contributed to our understanding of the chaperone cycle of the bacterial chaperone [[GroEL]]<ref name="Schmidt Rutkat Rachel Pfeifer pp. 656–659">{{cite journal | last1=Schmidt | first1=Marion | last2=Rutkat | first2=Kerstin | last3=Rachel | first3=Reinhard | last4=Pfeifer | first4=Günter | last5=Jaenicke | first5=Rainer | last6=Viitanen | first6=Paul | last7=Lorimer | first7=George | last8=Buchner | first8=Johannes | title=Symmetric Complexes of GroE Chaperonins as Part of the Functional Cycle | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=265 | issue=5172 | date=29 July 1994 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.7913554 | pages=656–659| pmid=7913554 | bibcode=1994Sci...265..656S }}</ref> and now lays a particular emphasis on [[Heat shock proteins|small heat shock proteins]] (sHsps), the [[Hsp90]] chaperone machinery and the role of molecular chaperones in [[antibody]] [[Protein folding|folding]]. Buchner's work established sHsps as molecular chaperones<ref name="Jakob Gaestel Engel Buchner pp. 1517–20">{{cite journal | last1=Jakob | first1=U | last2=Gaestel | first2=M | last3=Engel | first3=K | last4=Buchner | first4=J | title=Small heat shock proteins are molecular chaperones. | journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry | volume=268 | issue=3 | date=25 January 1993 | issn=0021-9258 | pmid=8093612 | pages=1517–20| doi=10.1016/S0021-9258(18)53882-5 | doi-access=free }}</ref> and has significantly contributed to our understanding of their function and mode of activation.<ref name="Haslbeck pp. 6744–6751">{{cite journal | last=Haslbeck | first=M. | title=Hsp26: a temperature-regulated chaperone | journal=The EMBO Journal | publisher=Wiley | volume=18 | issue=23 | date=1 December 1999 | issn=1460-2075 | doi=10.1093/emboj/18.23.6744 | pages=6744–6751| pmid=10581247 | pmc=1171736 }}</ref> His work on antibody folding delivered important insight in the mechanisms of how antibodies fold and are scrutinized by the cellular chaperone machinery.<ref name="Feige Groscurth Marcinowski Shimizu 2009 pp. 569–579">{{cite journal | last1=Feige | first1=Matthias J. | last2=Groscurth | first2=Sandra | last3=Marcinowski | first3=Moritz | last4=Shimizu | first4=Yuichiro | last5=Kessler | first5=Horst | last6=Hendershot | first6=Linda M. | last7=Buchner | first7=Johannes | title=An Unfolded CH1 Domain Controls the Assembly and Secretion of IgG Antibodies | journal=Molecular Cell | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=34 | issue=5 | year=2009 | issn=1097-2765 | doi=10.1016/j.molcel.2009.04.028 | pages=569–579| pmid=19524537 | pmc=2908990 }}</ref> A major focus of Johannes Buchner's lab is the Hsp90 chaperone machine. His work has provided a detailed mechanistic understanding of Hsp90 and its regulation by co-chaperones, establishing a functional chaperone cycle for Hsp90, which has become a major target in cancer therapy<ref name="Bose Weikl Bügl Buchner pp. 1715–1717">{{cite journal | last1=Bose | first1=Suchira | last2=Weikl | first2=Tina | last3=Bügl | first3=Hans | last4=Buchner | first4=Johannes | title=Chaperone Function of Hsp90-Associated Proteins | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=274 | issue=5293 | date=6 December 1996 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.274.5293.1715 | pages=1715–1717| pmid=8939863 | bibcode=1996Sci...274.1715B | s2cid=31998513 }}</ref><ref name="Hessling Richter Buchner pp. 287–293">{{cite journal | last1=Hessling | first1=Martin | last2=Richter | first2=Klaus | last3=Buchner | first3=Johannes | title=Dissection of the ATP-induced conformational cycle of the molecular chaperone Hsp90 | journal=Nature Structural & Molecular Biology | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=16 | issue=3 | date=22 February 2009 | issn=1545-9993 | doi=10.1038/nsmb.1565 | pages=287–293| pmid=19234467 | s2cid=25210016 }}</ref> Several discoveries from the Buchner lab on chaperone-mediated protein folding have been successfully translated into novel applications in biotechnology.

==Memberships and awards==
Buchner is a member of the [[Bavarian Academy of Sciences]], the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|German Academy of Sciences]] and was from 2015 to  2016 president of the German Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.<ref>[https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Johannes_Buchner_EN.pdf CV Leopoldina]</ref> Furthermore, he is a founding member of the Rainer Rudolph foundation. His work on protein folding and molecular chaperones has received several awards, among others the [[Hans Neurath]] Award of the [[Protein Society]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.proteinsociety.org/protein-society-awards/the-hans-neurath-award/ |title=The Protein Society: The home for the international protein science community |accessdate=3 March 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305020227/http://www.proteinsociety.org/protein-society-awards/the-hans-neurath-award/ |archivedate=5 March 2016 }}</ref> (2011), the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]] [[Schleiden Medal]] (2015), the [[Albrecht Kossel|Albrecht-Kossel]]-Award (2016) and the [[Max Bergmann]] Medal (2017).
